sonnet.problem: The wrong answer 'It carries him after his men' is nonsensical. Daniel's strength can't carry him anywhere, and the men ran off. It is a silly distractor and doesn't match the other answers in kind.
sonnet.rule: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

sonnet.problem: Card 1 says only that Daniel's words were heard and leaves out 'from the first day'. Nothing earlier lets the baker reason whether they were heard before or after the three weeks, so the pick is luck.
sonnet.rule: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

sonnet.problem: 'Who opposed him?' is ambiguous. 'Him' could be Daniel or the one sent to him, and the question's own sentence mentions both.
sonnet.rule: "He," "she" and "they" always point to someone the baker can tell.

sonnet.problem: Papa Dorin calls the twenty-one days of opposition 'the same stretch Daniel spent mourning.' The text only gives matching lengths and never says the two periods are the same or overlap.
sonnet.rule: Leave open what the text leaves open. Who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

sonnet.problem: Card 13 says the man 'strengthens him', which gives away the answer 'because you have strengthened me'. It also rules out the wrong answers about needing rest or breath.
sonnet.rule: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later. ... A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

sonnet.problem: Card 20 gives an outside passage (Daniel 5:31) a card of its own, restating Darius the Mede and adding the 'story isn't over' line. Outside passages are meant to ride along in a few words on a card that tells this passage.
sonnet.rule: An outside passage, like a New Testament fulfillment, only rides along in a few words on a card that tells this passage. It never gets a card of its own
